skill.name: worktree-manager-skill
skill.description: Manage Git worktrees for parallel development by creating, listing, removing, and troubleshooting isolated local environments.
skill.summary: Create, inspect, and remove Git worktrees with isolated ports and configuration.
skill.author: EGAdams

security_audit.summary: The static findings are mostly false positives from documentation examples, localhost URLs, slash command names, and .env references. I found no prompt injection attempt or evidence of credential exfiltration. One medium semantic risk remains because troubleshooting guidance includes manual force-kill and directory removal steps.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before killing processes or removing directories. Show the resolved path or PID and prefer /remove_worktree when possible.
State that .env values remain local, secret values must not be shown in responses, and only required port fields should be edited.
Document how managed processes are identified so cleanup does not stop unrelated services using similar ports.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Cleanup Guidance
semantic_findings.description: Troubleshooting guidance includes force-killing processes and manually removing orphaned worktree directories. These are legitimate recovery steps, but wrong targets could cause data loss or stop unrelated services.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines directly advise force-killing PIDs and using rm -rf on worktree paths. The context is troubleshooting, so the concern is data-loss risk rather than malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Parallel development can create branch, port, and cleanup confusion. This skill guides Git worktree creation, listing, removal, and troubleshooting with isolated local settings.
actual_capabilities: Selects create, list, or remove workflows from user intent.
Documents slash command syntax for worktree creation, listing, and removal.
Explains port offset allocation for server and client services.
Summarizes worktree status, service state, PIDs, and local access URLs.
Provides troubleshooting steps for port conflicts, orphaned worktrees, dependencies, and database configuration.
limitations: Relies on existing slash commands and does not implement them inside this skill.
Requires a repository that supports the expected worktree commands.
Removal workflows can affect local files and running processes.
Environment file values still require careful secret handling.

use_cases.title: Create Parallel Feature Environments
use_cases.description: Set up a separate worktree with unique ports for a feature branch.

use_cases.title: Review Active Worktrees
use_cases.description: List worktrees, service status, ports, and access URLs before changing local environments.

use_cases.title: Clean Up Completed Branch Worktrees
use_cases.description: Remove old worktrees and stop their related services after work is merged.

prompt_templates.title: List Current Worktrees
prompt_templates.prompt: Show my current worktrees, their service status, ports, and local access URLs.

prompt_templates.title: Create Feature Worktree
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a worktree for the feature-auth branch and tell me the dashboard and server URLs.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Port Conflict
prompt_templates.prompt: My worktree has a port conflict. Check existing worktrees and suggest the safest next action.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Multiple Environments
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a plan for three branch worktrees with unique port offsets and cleanup steps after review.

output_examples.output: The assistant identifies the branch, starts the creation workflow, and reports the worktree path, local URLs, and assigned ports.
The assistant lists each worktree, highlights running or stopped services, and notes any port conflicts.
The assistant confirms the target, runs the removal workflow, and reports stopped services and cleanup results.

best_practices: Confirm the target branch before creating or removing a worktree.
Use the list workflow before cleanup so ports, paths, and service state are visible.
Keep environment files local and avoid sharing secret values in responses.
anti_patterns: Do not run manual delete commands before validating the worktree path.
Do not reuse port offsets when another worktree is active.
Do not expose .env values when summarizing configuration.

faq.question: Does this skill run git commands directly?
faq.answer: It routes users to documented slash commands. The skill documentation says to avoid manual git worktree commands.

faq.question: Can it create a worktree with custom ports?
faq.answer: Yes. The create workflow accepts an optional port offset for server and client port allocation.

faq.question: Can it remove running services?
faq.answer: Yes. The removal workflow stops managed services and removes the selected worktree.

faq.question: Does it send data to external services?
faq.answer: No evidence found in the reviewed files. The documented URLs are localhost examples.

faq.question: What should I check before deletion?
faq.answer: List worktrees first, confirm the branch, verify the path, and review related service status.

faq.question: Which tools are supported?
faq.answer: The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
